name: Plansee
kurzbeschreibung: Lake Plansee near Reutte is Tirol's second-largest lake at 2.87 km², cradled fjord-like in the Ammergau Alps with crystalline waters, heritage boat cruises, and diving spots.
preis: Lakeshore and trails freely accessible; passenger boat cruises, watercraft rentals, and parking apply fees
oeffnungszeiten: Shoreline paths open year-round; passenger shipping operates late May to mid-October
beschreibung:
Überblick

The magnificent Lake Plansee near Reutte and Breitenwang in the Außerfern district covers 2.87 square kilometres, ranking as Tirol's second-largest natural lake after Lake Achensee. Resting at an elevation of 976 metres between the soaring limestone scarps of the Ammergau Alps, this alpine reservoir plunges to remarkable depths of 78 metres with a distinctly fjord-like profile. Renowned for its drinking-water purity and underwater visibility extending up to 15 metres, the lake shimmers in radiant shades from light turquoise to deep marine blue. A navigable 300-metre canal links Plansee seamlessly with neighboring Lake Heiterwanger See. Dense coniferous forests and sheer dolomite walls plunge directly into the mirror surface. As a premier alpine recreation destination, Plansee attracts scuba divers, sailors, paddleboarders, and walkers, while the historic motor vessels MS Margarethe and MS Wilhelm provide cherished scenic cruises.

Route & Anforderungen

Hikers at Lake Plansee enjoy a rich variety of scenic routes. Circling the entire lake along the wild southern shoreline path and the northern bank covers roughly 14 kilometres, taking about 3.5 to 4 hours of walking time (approx. 100 metres elevation change). The singletrack along the south bank hugs the water through pristine pine woodlands, unlocking panoramic vistas across secluded shingle beaches. Ambitious walkers can combine both lakes for an epic 20-kilometre alpine loop (approx. 5 to 6 hours walking time), utilizing passenger boats to shorten legs if desired. Sturdy trekking boots with deep tread are strongly recommended for the root-strewn south bank (inaccessible for strollers). The northern road provides gentle strolling terrain for families with buggies.

Besuch & Anreise

Motorists arrive via federal highway B179 to Reutte and proceed via Breitenwang along provincial road L255 directly along the lake basin. Dedicated paid parking bays are positioned along the northern road and near Hotel Forelle. Train travelers arrive at Reutte in Tirol station, connecting with seasonal valley buses directly to lakeshore stops.

Tipps

Embark on a scenic boat cruise aboard the motor vessels MS Margarethe or MS Wilhelm, which navigate the narrow channel into Lake Heiterwanger See. On balmy summer days, the secluded gravel bays along the south shore offer an exhilarating swim in drinking-quality alpine waters framed by limestone crags.
